# Microsoft 365 Connector Acceptance

## Research and status

- State: Approved with documented limitations
- Approval: User approved on 2026-09-03
- Connector: Microsoft Work IQ MCP 1.0.0
- Publisher: Microsoft
- Authentication: Brokered delegated login succeeded for the user's organizational account
- Installation: Package was initially inspected in OS temporary storage; workspace MCP configuration uses a pinned `npx` package version
- EULA: User reviewed the published package terms and explicitly authorized acceptance
- Agent tool boundary: `m365.agent.md` exposes only `workiq/ask`

The Work IQ MCP server also exposes create, update, delete, and action tools. They are excluded from this agent. The M365 agent must not be given generic entity or mutation tools.

## Architecture decision

Initial narrow Teams testing showed that Work IQ semantic search can cross Teams, meetings, email, and SharePoint/OneDrive-backed artifacts. Its documented capability filter was not reliably enforced for a unique no-result query. Because Microsoft 365 artifacts naturally cross product storage boundaries, the user approved one broad `m365` source agent replacing separate Teams, Outlook, SharePoint, Loop, and Planner agents.

Azure DevOps and Power BI remain separate source agents.

## Initial real-scope results

- Scope: User-provided CAE TPM meeting-recap phrase
- Discovery/factual lookup: Five bounded, relevant results with people, timestamps, deep links, and partial-coverage disclosure
- Reviewer result: Relevant
- Signals: Positive and negative inferences returned with citations and confidence labels
- Commitments/actions: Five explicit items returned with owner/date qualification and citations
- Source-system writes: None observed
- Repository persistence: No retrieved content written
- Temporary output: Deleted after review

Do not record retrieved content, names, excerpts, IDs, or links in this acceptance file.

## Known limitations to validate

- Semantic matching is fuzzy and may return relevant-looking records for a nonexistent marker.
- Search does not prove exhaustive recall.
- `ask` chooses retrieval strategy internally, so source and time coverage disclosures must be tested for accuracy.
- Citations can point to Teams, meetings, SharePoint/OneDrive artifacts, and other Microsoft 365 locations.
- Result bounding is instruction-driven; verify that oversized output is not returned.
- Loop and Planner coverage must be proven independently.
- Source comments and version/activity history are excluded by policy unless explicitly requested.

Accepted limitation on 2026-09-03:

- An exact-marker `ask` returned the correct `NOT_FOUND` visible answer and coverage qualification.
- Its structured response still included five unrelated, uncited internal reference records and sensitivity metadata.
- The user explicitly accepted this metadata exposure rather than adding a local sanitizing wrapper.
- The agent must ignore and never reproduce uncited references.

## Required scenarios

- [x] Customer/topic discovery and matching from flexible clues
- [x] Known-record factual lookup and reviewer relevance check
- [x] Positive and negative signal extraction
- [x] Commitment, action, owner, and date extraction
- [x] Exact no-result visible behavior using `ask`
- [x] Partial-result and no-result behavior; authentication succeeded
- [ ] Permission-denied and service-error paths not yet observed
- [x] Teams-specific coverage
- [x] Outlook-specific coverage
- [x] SharePoint-specific coverage
- [x] Loop limitation characterized; support removed by user decision
- [x] Planner-specific coverage, with poor relevance documented

## Hard gates

- [x] Delegated current-user identity only
- [x] Agent allowlist excludes mutation tools
- [x] Zero observed source-system writes
- [x] Bounded progressive history behavior
- [x] Item-level citations and available deep links in initial scenarios
- [x] Least-data behavior accepted with documented uncited-metadata and Planner exceptions
- [x] Coverage and recall limitations consistently disclosed
- [x] No retrieved content persisted in Git
- [x] Reviewed temporary data deleted
- [ ] Direct invocation through the VS Code repository agent requires a post-reload smoke test
- [x] Source-agent contract conformance with documented connector exceptions
- [x] User reviewed final results and explicitly approved

## Workload coverage results

- Teams: Relevant meeting, message, signal, commitment, action, timestamp, person, and deep-link results returned.
- Outlook: Relevant email and calendar results returned with item metadata, deep links, partial-result disclosure, and no message bodies.
- SharePoint/OneDrive: Relevant indexed document metadata and snippets returned with deep links and explicit non-exhaustive coverage.
- Loop: One relevant record was positively identified as Loop; workspace/page recall was partial.
- Planner: Retrieval worked, but no shared CAE TPM plan was found. It returned unrelated private tasks, so relevance/minimization failed for that query. The agent now requires an explicit relationship and must prefer no relevant result over fuzzy Planner matches.

### Narrow Loop validation

- Search required positive Loop evidence and excluded ordinary SharePoint/Office, email, meeting, recording, and Teams records.
- Result: one qualifying item returned with its actual title, `.loop` type, owner/modifier metadata, timestamp, factual description, explicit type evidence, and a `loop.cloud.microsoft` deep link.
- No additional records met both the supplied topic scope and Loop-identification criteria.
- Result was bounded, read-only, and disclosed indexing/access limitations.
- The reusable Loop qualification workflow is now part of `m365.agent.md`.

### Personal Loop workspace validation

- A search using four exact anchors supplied by the user discovered a personal Loop file and matched only the `NGA` anchor.
- Work IQ could not verify the remaining exact phrases from indexed content.
- Passing the discovered direct Loop URL back through Work IQ file grounding did not open the page; it returned only a linking record.
- Conclusion: personal Loop item discovery works in some cases, but full page-content retrieval is not reliable through the current `ask` surface.
- Agent behavior: report the discovery/content distinction, never guess missing page content, and treat pasted Loop text as user-provided evidence.
- Retry condition: Work IQ adds reliable Loop page-content grounding, or a separately approved read-only Loop/SharePoint Embedded content API becomes available.

Final Loop decision:

- Loop workspace-page support was removed by user decision on 2026-09-03.
- Work IQ discovery evidence remains documented only to explain the unsupported status.
- Loop and OneNote were removed from the planned source set by user decision.

No retrieved titles, people, IDs, excerpts, or links are retained here.
